what happens if date of the system changes after configuring?
basically we need to make sure date and time correct before User password expiration configured?

Could you please elaborate more on this? Because I do not understand what can be done or should be done in case if system time changes after password expiration has been set.
So far, there is a check in the code verifying that we do not set password expiration to a time point in the past. It is mentioned in steps 5 and 8 in 'Tested' section. Also, it is implemented in unit-tests as well.
ok, I mean suppose system has old time while configuring password expiration and then user set correct time.

I still might be not following you. So let me provide an example:
1. a user is created today (4th of Dec)
2. password expiration time for the user is set to the 5th of Dec
3. time inside BMC is switched to the 6th of Dec
4. now the password is expired 

It seems to be correct. Do you see a problem here?

this case is ok. but what if system has old date and time ex: 1971 jan 01
password expiration does not work as expected right?

I see your point now. Lets see what I've checked so far:
1. disable ntp in BMC: ```timedatectl set-ntp 0```
2. set date-time to the past: ```date -s '1971-01-01 11:30:30'``, ```hwclock --systohc```
3. create new user with a password expiration set to 'Wednesday, October 7, 2026 10:10:15 AM UTC': ```busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager /xyz/openbmc_project/user xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager CreateUser2 sassbt "user1" 1 "redfish" "priv-admin" true 1791367815```
4. check user info via ```chage```: ```chage -l user1```
```Last password change					: Jan 01, 1971
Password expires					: never
Password inactive					: never
Account expires						: never
Minimum number of days between password change		: 0
Maximum number of days between password change		: 20368
Number of days of warning before password expires	: 7```
5. verify that user is able to login to BMC via ssh
6. change date-time to the current time: ```date -s '2024-12-12 11:30:30'``, ```hwclock --systohc```
7. verify that user is able to login to BMC via ssh
8. ```chage``` starts to report incorrect information about password expiration here because of its internal code: ```chage -l user1```
```Last password change					: Jan 01, 1971
Password expires					: never
Password inactive					: never
Account expires						: never
Minimum number of days between password change		: 0
Maximum number of days between password change		: 20368
Number of days of warning before password expires	: 7```
9. change date-time to the future: ```date -s '2027-12-12 11:30:30'```, ```hwclock --systohc```
10. verify that password is expired, user is not able to login via ssh and gets error ```You are required to change your password immediately (password expired).```
11. ```chage``` still reports wrong information about password expiration: ```chage -l user1```
```Last password change					: Jan 01, 1971
Password expires					: never
Password inactive					: never
Account expires						: never
Minimum number of days between password change		: 0
Maximum number of days between password change		: 20368
Number of days of warning before password expires	: 7```

Weak place here is a date of the last password change, if password changes, then it shifts, so password expiration date-time shifts to the future as well, because ```chage``` operates on number of days since the last password change. Unfortunately, password expiration does not work in this case.
